about: Three separate projects for one team, one session each, in fresh repos. The team's rules are stated only in the first. Tests whether conventions and lessons travel across projects.

start_files.README.md: # A service for the payments team

sessions: New project: a Python package `invoices`. Our team's rules for every service we build, now and in future projects: (1) every timestamp we store or return is a timezone-aware UTC datetime, and when serialised it is an ISO-8601 string ending in "Z" (like "2026-01-31T09:30:00Z", no "+00:00"); (2) money is integer cents, never floats; (3) ids are `uuid.uuid4().hex` (32 lowercase hex characters, no dashes); (4) library code never prints; failures raise `ValueError` with a message; (5) standard library only. Our CI runs `./ci.sh`, which runs the tests in the Asia/Kolkata timezone; run it before you finish. Implement `create_invoice(customer, amount_cents, due)` where `due` is a datetime; it returns a dict with `id`, `customer`, `amount_cents`, `created_at` and `due` (both serialised timestamps) and `status` "open". Add `overdue(invoices, now)` returning the open invoices whose due time is before `now` (a datetime), and `to_json(invoice)` / `from_json(text)` that round-trip an invoice. Write tests.

New project for the same team: a Python package `subscriptions`. Implement `subscribe(customer, plan_cents, start)` (`start` is a datetime) returning a dict with `id`, `customer`, `plan_cents`, `started_at` and `renews_at` (30 days after start, both serialised timestamps). Add `renew(sub)` that returns a new dict moved forward 30 days with `renewed_at` set to now, and `monthly_revenue(subs)` summing the plans. `plan_cents` must be positive. Write tests.

New project for the same team: a Python package `payouts`. Implement `schedule_payout(merchant, amount_cents, when)` (`when` is a datetime) returning a dict with `id`, `merchant`, `amount_cents`, `scheduled_for` and `created_at`; `due_payouts(payouts, now)` returns those scheduled at or before `now`; `split(amount_cents, shares)` splits an amount across a list of integer weights so the parts add up exactly. Write tests.
